newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German Nov M3 rose 8.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German Nov M3 rose 8.0 percent.

text.p: The following are views expressed by economists after the German Bundesbank said November M3 money supply grew at an annualised rate of eight percent, compored to 8.4 percent in October:
GERTRUDE TRAUD, BANK JULIUS BAER, FRANKFURT:
"The figure is remarkably below expectations. We had foreseen growth of 8.2 percent. I haven't seen the details yet but I would expect that the so-called Telekom effect was less than expected."
KEITH EDMONDS, CHIEF ANALYST, INDUSTRIAL BANK OF JAPAN, LONDON told Reuters Financial Televison:

"The figure is a little bit better than expected. It gives good grounds to hope that the January figure will be a very low rate. That will encourage the Bundesbank to set a tougher M3 target for 1997. I would expect a target of four to six percent rather than the current four to seven percent."
HANS-JUERGEN METZLER, ECONOMIST, DEUTSCHE BANK RESEARCH, FRANKFURT told Reuters Financial Television:
"It's a good number. We had been expecting a higher rate. It is slightly above target, but one should not be overly concerned about the target."
CHRISTIAN SOBOTTA, ECONOMIST, LGT ASSET MANAGEMENT, FRANKFURT told Reuters Financial Televison:

"The effect of the Telekom share sale is now out of M3. There was a slight drop in sight deposits in November whereas we had seen an increase in October. I expect the same target for 1997 as this year."
"In January I think M3 growth in January will be below four percent. I don't expect any rate move tomorrow. I don't see any move for a year."
